hardware: Intel Core i7-12700H, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop 6 GB (held near 250 MHz by power and thermal limits)

proposals.statement: Parents struggle to get information from the school because fee statements are printed and sent home in learners' bags but half never reach parents

evidence.quote: Fee statements are printed every month and sent home in the learners' bags, and half of them never reach the parents.

proposals.statement: Parents call the school about fees they didn't know they owed

evidence.quote: Then I have parents phoning me about fees they didn't know they owed.

proposals.statement: Reports are printed, put in envelopes, and sent home but take a week of admin staff's time every term for 900 learners

evidence.quote: Reports are printed, put in envelopes, sent home. For about nine hundred learners that's a week of the admin staff's time every term.

proposals.statement: Notices like sports fixtures or school closures go on WhatsApp broadcast lists and email but parents who change numbers fall off the lists

evidence.quote: Those go on WhatsApp broadcast lists, and by email. But a broadcast list fills up, so we have five of them now, and parents who change their numbers just fall off.

proposals.statement: Parents need a single place to see what they owe, their child's reports, and school notices, and report their child's sickness

evidence.quote: One place where a parent can see what they owe, their child's reports and the school's notices, and tell us when their child is sick.

proposals.statement: The system must provide term reports as PDFs released on the same day for all parents

evidence.quote: The term report as a PDF, the same one we print. Released on the same day for everyone.

proposals.statement: Parents who change their contact numbers fall off WhatsApp broadcast lists and email lists, causing them to miss communications

evidence.quote: Those go on WhatsApp broadcast lists, and by email. But a broadcast list fills up, so we have five of them now, and parents who change their numbers just fall off.

proposals.statement: Parents pay school fees via EFT or debit order, not through the portal

evidence.quote: We don't take card payments and we're not going to, so there's no paying through the portal. Parents pay by EFT or debit order, like now.

proposals.statement: The system must show the current balance and monthly fee statements as PDFs for parents

evidence.quote: The current balance, the monthly statement as a PDF, and the reference to use for EFT.

proposals.statement: Absenteeism is tracked through handwritten notes in homework diaries or emails to teachers, who may not forward the information to the office

evidence.quote: Handwritten in the learner's homework diary, or an email to the class teacher, who may or may not pass it on to the office.

proposals.statement: A learner marked absent for three days was not communicated to the office due to current processes

evidence.quote: We had a learner marked absent for three days last term and nobody at the office knew why.

proposals.statement: The project must eliminate printing costs and time spent on paper-based processes

evidence.quote: And for us to stop printing. That's a real cost, and a lot of hours.

proposals.statement: The parent portal experiences performance issues when generating report PDFs for all 1400 parent contacts due to high concurrent logins within hours of report release.

evidence.quote: That day is the problem. When reports come out, every parent logs in within a couple of hours, mostly in the evening. We've got about fourteen hundred parent contacts. Last year we put one grade's reports on the website as a test, and the site fell over.

proposals.statement: The college uses SchoolBase 7, an internal server-based system from approximately 2014 that manages learners, parents, fees, and marks, and generates report PDFs.

evidence.quote: On a server in the admin block. It's SchoolBase 7, from about 2014 I think. It holds the learners, the parents, fees and marks. It can export to CSV, and it produces the report PDFs.

proposals.statement: The college does not have an API for SchoolBase to enable data synchronization between SchoolBase and the parent portal.

evidence.quote: Not that I know of. I've asked the supplier and they haven't answered yet.

proposals.statement: The parent portal's performance degrades when handling simultaneous requests from 1400 parent contacts logging in within a few hours after report release.

evidence.quote: When reports come out, every parent logs in within a couple of hours, mostly in the evening. We've got about fourteen hundred parent contacts. Last year we put one grade's reports on the website as a test, and the site fell over.

proposals.statement: The portal must only allow a learner's own parents or guardians to see their records

evidence.quote: Only a learner's own parents or guardians may see anything about that learner.

proposals.statement: The portal must allow for court-ordered exclusions where one parent cannot see records for some learners

evidence.quote: one of them may not see anything at all. There's a court order on about a dozen files.

proposals.statement: How out of date the parent balances would be if the portal uses a nightly CSV export from SchoolBase

evidence.quote: I'd want to know how out of date the balances would be.

proposals.statement: The portal should have small pages and only download PDFs when opened

evidence.quote: the portal has to be light: small pages, and the PDFs only downloaded when someone actually opens one.

proposals.statement: The portal could be zero-rated by the network to reduce data costs for parents

evidence.quote: could it be zero-rated? I heard some schools have arranged that with the networks.

proposals.statement: The portal must be light to accommodate parents on prepaid mobile data

evidence.quote: Most parents would use the portal on their phones rather than a computer, but honestly, we'd need to check.

proposals.statement: The portal must support isiZulu language for notices and main screens to accommodate grandparents who are more comfortable in isiZulu

evidence.quote: English is the school's language, but a lot of our grandparents look after the children, and they're more comfortable in isiZulu. If the notices and the main screens could be in isiZulu too, that would mean a lot.

proposals.statement: The portal must have large, clear text and be accessible to screen readers for parents with visual impairments

evidence.quote: And big, clear text. Some of our parents struggle with their eyesight, and we have a blind parent on the PTA who uses a screen reader.

proposals.statement: The portal must use the school's maroon color scheme instead of generic blue

evidence.quote: Oh, and please use the school's maroon, not some generic blue.

proposals.statement: The client has only one IT person who works two days a week, so if the portal breaks during report night, there's no one to fix it.

evidence.quote: Me, honestly. I'm the only IT person, and only two days a week. If something breaks on report night, there's nobody.

proposals.statement: The consultant proposed a trial with grade eight's term one reports in April to test the portal before full rollout.

evidence.quote: I'd suggest a trial with one grade's term one reports first.
Let's do grade eight in April as the trial.

proposals.statement: The client wants parents to receive two reports through the portal by the twenty-sixth of June.

evidence.quote: The term two reports go out on the twenty-sixth of June. We'd like parents to get those through the portal.

proposals.statement: The client uses SchoolBase for parent contacts, which has approximately sixteen hundred and fifty entries.

evidence.quote: Ayanda, I've just looked in SchoolBase while we were talking. It's not fourteen hundred parent contacts, it's about sixteen hundred and fifty.

proposals.statement: The client has only two days a week for IT work, so the portal must be designed to avoid breaking during report night.

evidence.quote: Me, honestly. I'm the only IT person, and only two days a week. If something breaks on report night, there's nobody.
